question_mappings.claim_scope: Initial diagnostic checks for click/no-crank should include battery condition and cable/terminal integrity before condemning the starter.
Rested open-circuit voltage for a conventional fully charged 12 V lead-acid battery.
Conditional carbon-pile load-test threshold tied to load magnitude, duration, and battery temperature.
Loaded voltage-drop testing helps locate excessive resistance in starter cables and connections.
Corrosion or loose/damaged connections can increase resistance and reduce starter-circuit performance.
Excessive ground-path voltage drop can cause slow crank or no crank under load.
Starter control-circuit checks should use the wiring/service procedure and voltage-based diagnosis while energized.
Starter/IMS control voltage must be interpreted against the applicable circuit design and service specification.
Start-request path may involve switch/input/module/network/wiring depending on design.
Valid Park/Neutral or transmission-range input may be required for starter authorization.
Vehicles equipped with a clutch-start interlock may inhibit cranking when the input is invalid.
Starter current draw is not independently diagnostic and must be interpreted with the wider starting-system condition and applicable specification.
Suspected engine mechanical lockup should be verified with an approved mechanical procedure while the vehicle is safely disabled.
Security/immobilizer behavior is vehicle-specific and may or may not inhibit crank.
Correct circuit documentation is needed to identify control and power-path checks.
Starter command/crank request/enable scan data are manufacturer/model dependent.
Battery/starter cable and terminal condition should be visually inspected for corrosion, damage, and connection issues.
Improvised bypassing can defeat safety interlocks or circuit protection; manufacturer-approved test methods should be used.
Post-repair verification should confirm the original symptom is corrected and repeat the relevant diagnostic checks.
Starter drive/pinion/ring-gear engagement faults can require inspection after starter diagnosis.
